facts.fact: Maungawhau is 196 metres high and Auckland’s highest volcano; it is also a significant Māori pā site.
facts.excerpt: At 196m tall, Maungawhau or Mount Eden is the highest volcano in Auckland.

facts.fact: Historic living and working terraces and crop-storage pits preserve evidence of the pā layout.
facts.excerpt: On the outer slopes there are numerous flat terraces used mainly for living and working space.

facts.fact: The summit road and tihi have been closed to private vehicles, including motorcycles and scooters, since January 2016.
facts.excerpt: closed to private motor vehicles, including motorbikes and scooters, in January 2016.

facts.fact: The boardwalk protects surviving pā features; visitors should use authorised routes rather than shortcuts over archaeological terraces.
facts.excerpt: The boardwalk provides long overdue protection for the historic features that are the last remnants of the pā

facts.fact: The authority’s project text requires visitors to follow current signs and staff instructions. No claim is made that the dated project is complete.
facts.excerpt: please follow all onsite signage and instructions from construction staff.

facts.fact: The site is on a tentative UNESCO list; the article makes no claim of an existing World Heritage inscription.
facts.excerpt: is on a tentative list for UNESCO World Heritage status
